resources.title: The Hijrah to Yathrib (Madinah)
resources.description: Theme: SIRAH JS ONE | Content: (a) The meaning of Hijrah. (b) Circumstances of the Hijrah. (c) The significance of the Hijrah.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: (a) State the circumstances that led to the Hijrah. (b) Describe how the Hijrah occurred. (c) Explain how the Prophet and the Muslims were received in Madinah. (d) Explain the significance of the Hijrah.
resources.activities:
Teacher: (a) Gives reasons and circumstances that led to Hijrah. (b) Narrates the story of the Hijrah. (c) Draws the students through questioning to some of the lessons of the Hijrah.

Students: (a) Listen to the teacher’s narrations. (b) Participate in the discussions. (c) Mention some of the lessons of the Hijrah.
resources.resources: (a) A map showing the route of the Hijrah from Makkah to Madinah and location of cave Thawr. (b) Information Technology Devices
resources.assessment: Students to: (a) Explain the meaning of Hijrah and circumstances that led to it. (b) Describe how the Hijrah was performed. (c) Explain three lessons derived from the Hijrah. (d) Explain the significance of Hijrah.

resources.title: Effects of the Hijrah
resources.description: Theme: SIRAH JS ONE | Content: (a) Building of Masjid an- Nabawi (b) Rehabilitation of the Muhajirun (c) Foundation of the Ummah (d) The battles.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: (a) State the various steps taken by the Prophet (SAW). (b) Mention the three major battles. (c) Identify the circumstances that led to each battle. (d) State the lessons derived from the foundation of the Ummah and the three major battles.
resources.activities:
Teacher: (a) Narrates the various steps taken by the Prophet to establish the Ummah in Madinah. (b) Explains the circumstances that led to the three major battles. (c) States the lessons derived from the foundation of the Ummah and the three battles. (d) Encourages the students to put the lessons into practice.

Students: (a) Listen to the story. (b) Mention some of the steps used by the Prophet in establishing the Ummah. (c) State the circumstances that led to each of the major battles. Identify some lessons derived from the foundation of the Ummah and the battles.
resources.resources: (a) A diagram of the city of Madinah. (b) A picture of the Prophet’s mosque. (c) Information Technology Devices
resources.assessment: Students to: (a) Narrate the various steps taken by the Prophet in establishing the Ummah in Madinah. (b) Explain the circumstances that led to the three major battles. (c) Mention five lessons derived from the battles.

resources.title: Conquest of Makkah
resources.description: Theme: SIRAH JS ONE | Content: What led to the conquest of Makkah.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: (a) State the circumstances which led to the conquest of Makkah in the 8th year of Hijrah. (b) Explain how the Prophet (SAW) conquered Makkah.
resources.activities:
Teacher: (a) Narrates the circumstances that led to the conquest of Makkah. (b) Explain how the Quraish violated the treaty which led to the conquest of Makkah. (c) Highlights the lessons derived and how to apply them in the daily life.

Students: (a) Listen to the teacher’s narration. (b) State the consequence of the violation. (c) Identify some of the lessons and how to apply them in the daily life.
resources.resources: (a) A map showing the location of Al- Hudaybiyyah, Makkah and Madinah. (b) Picture of Ka’abah (c) Information Technology Devices
resources.assessment: Students to: (a) Mention some of the circumstances that led to the conquest of Makkah. (b) Explain the manner in which the Quraish violated the treaty of hudaybiyah. (c) Mention four lessons and their applications in daily life.

resources.title: Child’s Basic Rights in Islam
resources.description: Theme: TAHDHIB JS ONE | Content: Survival rights
resources.objectives: Students should be able to recognize Child’s basic survival rights in Islam.
resources.activities:
Teacher: (a) Guides students to think about their rights (b) Guides to recognize the child’s right in Islam. (c) Uses some Qur’anic ayaat to support the rights. (d) Highlights the UNO convention on the rights of the child. (e) Explains how these rights are implemented.

Students: (a) Respond to teacher’s enquiries. (b) Listen to teacher’s explanation. (c) Discuss the Qur’anic verses and Hadith with the teacher. (d) Comment on UNO convention on their experience on the rights of the child. .
resources.resources: (a) Charts of Child rights. (b) Copy of the UNO convention on Child’s Basic Rights
resources.assessment: Students to list rights of child in Islam.

resources.title: Child’s Responsibiliti es to Allah
resources.description: Theme: TAHDHIB JS ONE | Content: (a) Ibadah (worship of Allah), (b) Obedience of Allah’s laws. (c) Obedience to the laws of Allah.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: (a) State child’s responsibilities to Allah. (b) Recite and explain the meaning of Child’s responsibilities to Allah. Q2:21 (c) Realize the reasons for human creation Q51: 56-58
resources.activities:
Teacher: (a) Guides students to recognize Allah’s bounties on them. (b) Guides to appreciate that, to whom much is given, much is expected. (c) Leads students to recognize that they have responsibilities towards Allah for all His bounties. (d) Guides them to understand that worship of Allah and obedience to His laws are parts of the child’s responsibilities toward Allah. (e) Makes use of Q2:21 to explain the topic.

Students: (a) Listen to teacher’s explanation. (b) List the bounties of Allah. (c) Commit Q2:21 to memory (d) Ask questions. (e) List child’s responsibilities to Allah. .
resources.resources: Charts containing the text of Q2:21, Q51:56-58 and their translation.
resources.assessment: Students to: (a) State their responsibilities to Allah. (b) Recite Q2:21 and Q51:56- 58 (c) Explain the meaning of Q2:21 and Q51:51-56

resources.title: Relationship Between Muslims and non-Muslims
resources.description: Theme: TAHDHIB JS ONE | Content: (a) Forgiveness Q24:22. (b) Tolerance Q60:8-9 (c) Kindness Q2:83
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: (a) State the need for forgiveness, tolerance and kindness in Islam. (b) Explain the need to forgive, to tolerate and be kind to others. (c) Explain the meaning of Qur’anic verses and Hadith on those virtues
resources.activities:
Teacher: (a) Guides students to explain what it takes to maintain cordial relationship. (b) Guides students to state that forgiveness, tolerance and kindness are the ingredients of maintaining good relationship with others. (c) Shows the importance of these virtues with reference to Qur’anic verses and Hadith.

Students: (a) Listen to teacher’s explanation. (b) List the significance of the virtuous acts. (c) Discuss their experience. (d) Discuss the meaning of the verses and Hadith.
resources.resources: Charts containing Qur’anic verses and Hadith on the virtuous acts.
resources.assessment: Students to: (a) State the need for forgiveness, tolerance and kindness as Islamic virtues. (b) Why should we imbibe the virtuous of forgiveness, tolerance and kindness. (c) Explain the meaning of Qur’anic verses

resources.title: Child’s Right in Islam (Development) II
resources.description: Theme: TAHDHIB JS ONE | Content: (a) Right to education. (b) Right to parental care. (c) Relevant Qur’anic verses (Q31 vs 13 – 19).
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: (a) Explain the meaning of Child’s right in Islam (b) Mention education and adequate care as basic rights (c) Discuss/explain that Islam requires Muslims to be educated and care ful.
resources.activities:
Teacher: (a) Guides the students to define what are development rights. (b) Guides them to recognize child development rights in Islam. (c) Leads them to discover that education is a child’s right in Islam. (d) Uses Qur’anic verses, Hadith and quotation from Sheikh Uthman bin Fodio to support his explanation. (e) Highlights the UNO convention on child’s rights as it relates to development rights. (f) Explains how those rights are implanted in the society.

Students: (a) to respond to teacher’s enquires. (b) Listen to teacher’s explanation. (c) Discuss the relevant verses, Hadith and quotations. (d) Ask questions.
resources.resources: A chart containing child’s development rights
resources.assessment: Students to: (a) Give five concept of child’s right in Islam. (b) List rights of the child in Islam. (c) Explain the meaning of verses, Hadith and the quotations. (d) Explain whether Islam requires Muslims to be educated and careful.

resources.title: Child’s Responsibilities to Parents and Relationship
resources.description: Theme: TAHDHIB JS ONE | Content: (a) Goodness to Parents. (b) Obedience to Parents. (c) Responsibilities to relations (Q30:38).
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: (a) State child’s responsibilities to their parents and relations. (b) Recite Q17:23 – 24, Q30:38 and their meanings.
resources.activities:
Teacher: (a) Guides students to recognize how their parents suffer for their sake. (b) Guides them to appreciate why they should show goodness to their parents and relations. (c) Leads them to appreciate that obedience and goodness to parents and relations are parts of ibadat (Obedience to Allah’s commandment) (d) Explains the meaning of the content of Q17:23 – 24, Q30:38. (e) Guides the students to commit the Qur’anic verses to memory.

Students: (a) Listen to teacher’s explanation. (b) Explain how parents suffer for the sake of their children. (c) Commit Q17:23-24 and Q30:38 to memory. (d) Lists child’s responsibilities to parents and relations. (e) Ask questions
resources.resources: A chart containing the text of Q17:23-24 and Q30:30
resources.assessment: Students to: (a) State five child’s responsibilities to their parents and relations. (b) Recite Q17:23 – 24, Q30:38.

resources.title: Human Relations I
resources.description: Theme: TAHDHIB JS ONE | Content: (a) Greetings (b) Responses. (c) Peaceful co- existence
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: (a) Explain the importance of various forms of greetings in Islam. (b) State how to exchange greetings in Islam. (c) State the significance of peaceful c0- existence among people irrespective of their religions (d) State the significance of exchanging greetings and goodwill messages among people irrespective of their religion..
resources.activities:
Teacher: (a) Greets the students and observe their responses. (b) Guides the students to greet and respond in Islamic way. (c) Explains the meaning of the expressions to the students. (d) Guides the students to discover that it is essential to reply when a Muslim is greeted by anybody irrespective of their religion. (e) Supports the point with Q4:86 and relevant Hadith.

Students: (a) Exchange greeting with the teacher. (b) Discuss the meaning of the greeting expressions with the teacher. (c) Commit Q4:86 to memory.
resources.resources: (a) A chart. (b) Information Technology Devices
resources.assessment: Ask the students to: (a) Explain the importance of various forms of greetings in Islam. (b) State how to exchange greetings in Islam. (c) State the significance of exchange gift and goodwill messages to non muslims (d) State the significance of exchanging greeting with non-Muslims.

resources.title: Islamic Greeting (As-salamu ’Alaykum or At-Tasleem)
resources.description: Theme: TAHDHIB JS ONE | Content: (a) As-Salamu Alaykum Warahmatu llahi Wabarakatuhu (b) Wa’alaykumussa lamu Warahmatullahi Wabarakatuhu
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: (a) Explain the importance of Islamic greeting (At- Tasleem). (b) State how to greet Islamically. (c) Pronounce the text of Islamic greeting correctly. (d) State the virtues and etiquettes of Islamic greeting. (e) Cite evidences on At- Tasleem (Islamic Greeting)
resources.activities:
Teacher: (a) Greets the students Islamically and observe their responses. (b) Guides the students on the correct way/text of Islamic greeting. (c) Demonstrates with some students how to extend greeting islamically. (d) States the virtues and etiquettes of Islamic greeting (e) Supports the points with Q4:86 and relevant Hadith.

Students: (a) Exchange greeting with the teacher. (b) Discuss the meaning of the greeting expressions with the teacher. (c) Commit Q4:86 to memory.
resources.resources: (a) A chart. (b) Information Technology Devices
resources.assessment: Students to: (a) Explain the importance of At-Tasleem (Islamic greeting). (b) Pronounce correctly the text or Islamic greeting. (c) Respond appropriately to whoever greet him/her Islamically. (d) State the virtues and etiquettes of “At-Tasleem” (e) Cite any relevant evidence on Islamic greeting.

resources.objectives: Students should be able to: (a) Narrate the brief history of Prophet ‘Isa (AS); (b) Deduce the lessons contained in his life. (c) Identify the ways in which these lessons could be reflected in the life of a Muslim
resources.activities:
Teacher: (a) Narrates the brief history of Prophet “Isa with special reference to: (i) His miraculous birth; (ii) His prophet hood (iii) His persecution by the Jews and their failure to crucify him; (iv) Revelation of Injiil to him and the loss of the original version of injiil. (v) Muslim’s respect for Prophet ‘Isa(AS);; (vi) State lessons deduced from the life of Prophet ‘Isa (AS) and the reflection of these in the life of a Muslim.

Students: (a) Listen to the teacher’s narration of Prophet ‘Isa (AS); (b) Explain briefly Prophet ‘Isa’s life history. (c) State lessons derived from his life history; (d) Mention ways of reflecting the lessons in the life of a Muslim.
resources.resources: (a) Q6:83 -90, Q3:45,55,84 etc. (b) Information technology devices.
resources.assessment: Students to: (a) Explain briefly the life history of Prophet ‘Isa (AS); (b) State lessons contained in Prophet ‘Isa’s life history; (c) Mention ways of reflecting the lessons in the life of a Muslim.

resources.title: Human Relations III
resources.description: Theme: TAHDHIB | Content: Neighbourliness
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: (a) Describe who is a neighbor; (b) Give examples of how to be a good neighbor; (c) State the Islamic injunctions on good neighbourliness.
resources.activities:
Teacher: (a) Guides the students to describe who is a neighbor from Islamic perspective. (b) Divide students into manageable groups to discuss good neighbourliness. (c) Facilitates and moderate group work; (d) Rounds up the group presentation with quotation from Q4: 36 and Q107: 4-7 and Hadith; (e) Encourages students to commit to memory Qur’anic verses and Hadith after displaying charts containing these quotations.

Students: (a) Describe who is a neighbor; (b) Participate in group work; (c) Listen to teacher’s presentation of quotation from Qur’an and Hadith. (d) Commit Qur’anic verses an Hadith into memory.
resources.resources: Charts containing Q4:36 and Q107:4-7
resources.assessment: Students to: (a) Describe who is a neighbor; (b) Give examples of how to be a good neighbor; (c) State the Islamic injunctions on good neighbourliness.

resources.title: Maintenance of Good Health in Islam II
resources.description: Theme: TAHDHIB | Content: (a) Lawful Food. (b) Unlawful Food. Q2:172 -173
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: (a) State foods which are lawful and unlawful for a Muslim. (b) Give circumstance when a Muslim is allowed to take food which are unlawful.
resources.activities:
Teacher: (a) Guides students to list various types of food they know. (b) Mentions other types of foods not listed by students. (c) Leads the students to classifying the listed foods into lawful and unlawful food. (d) Guides students to describe the correct method to slaughter animals in Islam. (e) Discuss circumstances under which a Muslim may be allowed to eat forbidden food. (f) Facilitates students’ group work to discuss lawful and unlawful foods. (g) Displays charts of lawful and unlawful foods.

Students: (a) Listen to the teacher attentively. (b) Classify foods into lawful and unlawful. (c) Participate in group work to discuss lawful and unlawful foods. (d) Present reports of group work. (e) Ask questions
resources.resources: (a) Charts on lawful and unlawful foods. (b) Real foods
resources.assessment: Students to: (a) Mention foods that are lawful. (b) Mention foods that are unlawful. (c) Give circumstances when a Muslim is allowed to take food which are forbidden.
